meaning:
φρυάσσω
(so Ps, l.with, NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Psa.2:1 (רָגַשׁ), 2Ma.7:34 R, 3Ma.2:2 * ;]
prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaphorical, to be wanton, insolent: Act.4:25 (LXX).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: who by the mouth of your servant, David, said, ‘Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?
